insights.insight: Every one of the 9,743 receipts in this network is a confirmed purchase event — not a behavioral inference. The ad industry pays $5+ CPM to guess who might buy; this protocol sells proof that someone already did.

insights.topic: Weekly GMV velocity as a targeting freshness indicator
insights.insight: The 7-day GMV window hit $208,920 as of April 10, up from roughly $100K just three days prior — meaning the signal pool is refreshing fast enough to support near-real-time audience activation, not just retrospective analysis.

The single largest GMV burst on record — $56,064 in one 4-hour cycle — was driven by only 42 new receipts, implying a cluster of high-basket-size transactions; for brands targeting premium or high-LTV buyers, this is the segment to watch.

April 9 marked the first non-physical-commerce category in network history, signaling the protocol is beginning to capture digital spend alongside retail; for CMOs, this opens the possibility of cross-domain attribution between software purchases and physical buying behavior.

The network reached 16 active CBSAs spanning major metros (NYC, LA, Miami, Seattle) and non-metro areas (Alabama, Idaho, Rhode Island), with velocity recovering to 1.037x even as two new markets were added — suggesting audience scale is building without sacrificing signal density in established markets.

insights.topic: Category diversity as a targeting surface
insights.insight: At 3.262 bits of category entropy, no single retail vertical dominates the receipt pool — grocery, home improvement, electronics, restaurant, and now SaaS all contribute, giving brand marketers a multi-category verified audience rather than a single-vertical panel.
